newsitem.title: CHINA: Shenzhen applies for foreign bank yuan business.
newsitem.headline: Shenzhen applies for foreign bank yuan business.

text.p: The Shenzhen branch of the People's Bank of China, the central bank, has applied to Beijing for permission to allow foreign banks to conduct local currency business, a central bank official said on Monday.

The start of yuan business by foreign banks needs the approval of China's State Council, or cabinet, the official in the southern boomtown told the Hong Kong-based newsletter China Securities Bulletin.
China has so far only given permission to nine foreign banks to conduct yuan business on a limited basis in Shanghai.

Shenzhen has been trying to gain central government approval to allow foreign banks to begin yuan business as soon as possible, the Shenzhen-based Securities Times recently quoted Shenzhen central bank president Jiang Chaoliang as saying.
Shenzhen authorities are also trying for approval to allow the establishment of Sino-foreign brokerages, investment funds and insurance firms, Jiang told a meeting of foreign bankers last week.
Shenzhen Communist Party Secretary Li Youwei said in April that China would allow foreign banks in Shenzhen to conduct domestic currency business.
Li said permission for the opening would be forthcoming but did not give a timetable, adding there were 52 foreign-funded banks in Shenzhen.

The newspaper said that by June 30 this year, the deposit balance of foreign-invested financial institutions in Shenzhen had reached more than US$800 million against a total loan balance of about US$4.1 billion.
